messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: prod-gpu-pool capacity exhausted in us-west-2. Autoscaler failing to add nodes. Impact: inference requests throttled / queue growth. Paging on-call: @raj :rotating_light:
raj: acked, joining. reading graphs now.
lucy: I'm pulling logs for autoscaler and scheduler. queue_length spiking to ~14k across model-route-prod-chat-1.
michael: seeing 503 spikes and client retries. CS reports some customers hitting latency >30s.
sarah: on call handoff in 30m, keep updates in thread.
ops-bot: Automatically created incident ticket INC-2026-117, link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-117
raj: quick check — is this pure capacity or a placement problem? any MIG fragmentation?
lucy: initial look: cluster has 10 nodes with GPUs but autoscaler logged repeated 'no nodes fit' when trying to create pods: ``Events: FailedScheduling  pod/chat-infer-xyz  0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient gpu.mig.slices``
michael: autoscaler logs show: ``scaleUp: need 8 GPUs but maxNodes=6, aborting``
carol: ugh, our autoscaler max_node config for prod-gpu-pool was 6 after last cost-saving change. that explains scale limits.
raj: can we temporarily bump max_nodes to 12? who's got permissions?
sarah: I can do it, have infra perms. doing now.
[code]
# bump autoscaler max
gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling prod-gpu-ig --max-num-replicas 12
kubectl get nodes -l pool=prod-gpu-pool
[/code]
sarah: changed to 12. autoscaler attempting to provision.
lucy: new nodes are provisioning but scheduler still failing to pack pods due to MIG sizes: some nodes are 1xA100-MIG-7g, others are 2xA100-MIG-3g; our pod requests are specific to gpu.mig=7g and can't fit on mixed.
michael: so we have stranded fractional capacity: nodes with 3g slices can't run 7g-requesting pods.
raj: thoughts: either relax pod requests to accept 3g (if model fits), or run binpacking to consolidate 7g workloads onto 7g nodes and drain 3g nodes.
carol: draining 3g nodes will be slow and cause extra evictions. also autoscaler created mixture due to AZ diversity.
lucy: suggestion: temporarily change model-mem-class to allow 3g variants for non-critical routes and shift high-throughput customers to 7g-only pool.
ops-bot: Note: severity P1 — customer-impacted. See runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/gpu-capacity.md
raj: we need immediate mitigation: 1) throttle low-priority requests, 2) move cached/cold-start responses, 3) enable model fallback to CPU for <512 token requests. can someone flip the throttle?
michael: I'm enabling rate-limiter rule now to reduce bursty QPS from non-paid routes.
[code]
# apply limiter
redwoodctl rate-limit create --route "*/guest/*" --rps 5 --duration 60s
[/code]
michael: rule in place. queue length down ~20% after 90s.
sarah: new nodes are up but scheduling still reports "node(s) had volume node-affinity" for some pods. checking PVs.
lucy: PV affinity was due to local SSD mount for model cache on some nodes. that's blocking cross-az scheduling. we can set cache to S3 for now to avoid PV constraints.
carol: switching cache to S3 for route model-cache-prod-chat. small config change, rolling restart needed.
[code]
# patch deployment to use s3 cache
kubectl set env deploy/chat-infer MODEL_CACHE=s3://prod-model-cache
kubectl rollout restart deploy/chat-infer
[/code]
carol: rolling restart started. expected ~3m to drain.
raj: monitoring: queue_length trending down but still higher than normal. throttling reduced customer error rate for paid customers.
michael: CS update sent: "We experienced degraded performance due to GPU scheduling constraints. We're applying mitigations; paid customers on dedicated capacity unaffected."
sarah: autoscaler note: provisioning rate was limited by regional quota, requested quota increase 30m ago, not approved yet. opened cloud support ticket.
ops-bot: Cloud support case CS-99845 opened.
lucy: important root cause: mixed MIG sizing + tight autoscaler max + PV locality created binpacking conflict that left 40% of GPUs stranded (can't host 7g pods).
raj: agree. longer-term fixes: (a) enforce homogeneous node pools per MIG size, (b) make pod resource requests flexible across MIG classes, (c) update autoscaler to consider binpacking score when selecting node type.
michael: adding short-term workaround: taint 3g nodes and create a cheaper route-level fallback to use CPU for small requests until compaction finished. who will own the compaction?
lucy: I'll drive compaction. plan: cordon 3g nodes, migrate 7g pods to new 7g-only nodes, then deprovision empty fragmented nodes. target window 45m.
carol: I'll handle cache S3 switchback if needed and watch evictions.
sarah: on-call handoff note: I'm on duty for next 30m then handoff to @michael. michael, I'm going to post current state & steps in the handoff channel.
michael: ack. I'll watch autoscaler and cloud quota.
raj: update customer impact: high latency for some public endpoints, a small portion of paid customers saw increased latency but no data loss. CS notified.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-117 severity remains P1. Current mitigations: rate-limiting guest traffic, bump autoscaler max to 12, S3 model cache fallback, cordon/compaction plan.
lucy: compaction started: cordoning nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-3g-02` then evicting non-critical pods.
[code]
kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-3g-02
kubectl drain gpu-node-3g-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
[/code]
lucy: migrated ~18 pods off gpu-node-3g-02. scheduler placed them on 7g nodes. freeing 3g capacity.
michael: cluster GPU utilization now 86% with available 7g slots appearing. queue length down to ~900.
raj: good. start deprovisioning empty nodes once pods stable. keep throttles until 30m after stable.
sarah: taking notes for postmortem: root causes, timeline, mitigation steps, follow-ups (enforce homogeneous pools, autoscaler policy change, PV locality audit, quota monitoring).
carol: I will update runbook with MIG sizing checklist and add a runbook step for switching cache to S3 to avoid PV lock.
ops-bot: Post-incident survey will be generated and assigned to participants.
michael: final check: any remaining customer-facing issues?
raj: CS says residual latency for small subset, but overall service recovering. I'll set incident to 'monitoring' in 15m if stable.
[10m later]
eng-oncall: monitoring window complete, metrics stable for 20m. queue length <200, error rates back to baseline.
raj: marking incident as resolved -> monitoring. creating follow-up ticket: TKT-2026-341 (compaction retrospective + autoscaler config change + quota escalation).
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-117 moved to status: resolved-monitoring.
sarah: handing off full writeup to follow-up owner. thanks all :clap:
